proof_summary: Direct exhaustive modular counts establish the first five minima. For the last, the congruence forces every counted divisor \(d\) to be unitary—otherwise a common prime factor of \(d\) and \(k/d\) would divide both \(d^{d-1}\) and \(d^{d-1}-1\)—so the count is at most \(2^{\omega(k)}\); a prime-factor sieve below \(2310\) leaves only the integers with at least four distinct prime factors, and finite modular computation excludes these candidates while showing that \(2310\) attains the required count.
